name: brief
shape: A published research brief. One argument, carried end to end.
template: Cover, up to two section openers, six to fourteen working pages, a source page.
measuredFrom: The strict published population of the ExampleSlides corpus: 51 confidently published decks, 2,744 working pages after excluding covers, dividers, agendas, disclaimers and closings. Census run 2026-08-26.
notes: These are research numbers, not client-deck numbers. A published research page carries FEWER words than a client deliverable (141 against 162) and its titles are SHORTER by three words at the median. Calibrating a research piece to the deliverable profile produces a page that is too full and a title that is too long.

thinShare is not a defect rate. 41% of published research pages run under 120 words, so a piece with two fifths of its pages thin is in line with the corpus rather than underfull. The deliverable profile treats a thin page as a warning because a client page under 120 words usually is a placeholder; here it is a form.
numberShareFloor is set below the median share rather than at it. A median is the middle of a distribution, so scoring every piece against it fails half of a well-calibrated corpus by construction.
